newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sumitomo files fraud complaint against ex-trader.
newsitem.headline: Sumitomo files fraud complaint against ex-trader.

text.p: Sumitomo Corp has filed a new complaint with Tokyo prosecutors against ex-copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka, alleging he committed fraud in connection with the firm's huge copper losses, a spokesman for the Japanese trading house said on Tuesday.

Tuesday's move follows an earlier complaint, issued by Sumitomo on October 21, alleging that Hamanaka forged documents relating to the firm's estimated $2.6 billion losses on world copper markets. Hamanaka was arrested the following day by Tokyo prosecutors for suspected forgery.

The latest complaint states that Hamanaka, former chief of the company's non-ferrous metals department, fraudulently raised $770 million through a Hong Kong subsidiary of Sumitomo for the alleged purpose of purchasing copper warrants.
It said he raised the funds, without the knowledge of his company, to cover losses from futures trading with overseas counterparts.

Hamanaka, once dubbed "Mr Five Percent" due to his rumoured control of a significant part of the global copper market, was fired in June when Sumitomo announced it had lost vast sums on what it called unauthorised copper trades. A lawyer representing Hamanaka has said that he has admitted forgery but denies manipulating world copper markets.
